## Relevant Symbols
- `hooks/ledger.sh:799` — publish is gated on `cfgp '.orchestrate.publish // false' = true`; the same idiom gates `publish_commit` (D2).
- `hooks/ledger.sh:817-818` — the stored body hash is checked BEFORE marking; a mismatch dies with "the board is untouched".
- `hooks/ledger.sh:820` — `MARKED=$(bash "$SB" --mark …)`; the only consumer of `--mark` stdout, which it matches for `*"not marked"*` (:823).
- `hooks/ledger.sh:821-822` — re-read + `record --body-file` re-hashes right after the mark; this must move after the commit (spec D4/FR-006).
- `hooks/ledger.sh:834-835` — `.published = {state, at}` is the last write; nothing earlier records the state.
- `hooks/status-board.sh:266-271` — the column loop; DONE returns `… not marked` before any path resolution.
- `hooks/status-board.sh:274` — `f=$(readlink -f … || resolve_link …)`: the resolved target is only known inside `mark_item`; a locate mode must reuse this exact resolution (FR-004).
- `hooks/status-board.sh:287` — success prints `marked <id> <m> in <column name>` — no path today.
- `hooks/board-lib.sh:119` — external ctx carries `board_top` (physical path); `ledger.sh:859` reads it as `jq -r .board_top <<<"$BCTX"`.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:352-363` — mkdir lock with a one-minute stale break; the pattern for a publish lock.

## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Sourced helper per concern, guarded by an existence check with a reinstall message (`ledger.sh:102-104`).
- Every refusal is `die "<command> <id>: <evidence> — <what to do>"` (`ledger.sh:799`, `:818`).
- Opt-in config read with `cfgp '<path> // false'` and compared to the literal `true` (`ledger.sh:799`).
- Smoke tests: a `*_fail=0` block per FR, `bad "…"` with the observed value, one `ok "… (spec FR-n)"` (`tests/smoke.sh:4062-4078`).
- Portable git/stat: GNU then BSD fallbacks (`status-board.sh:276`); macOS bash 3.2 (no associative arrays).

## Open Questions
- None blocking. Items answered from the code:
  - Does anything parse `--mark`'s output besides `publish`? No — `grep -rn -- --mark hooks commands` finds only `ledger.sh:820`; tests do not match `marked …` text. Adding a `path:` line is safe.
  - Is a new setup allowlist entry needed? No — `ledger.sh publish:*` (`hefesto-setup.sh:127`) covers the subcommand; git runs inside it.
  - Concurrency: two lanes publishing two items in the SAME column file could interleave mark/commit (B's marker swept into A's commit, or A's rollback erasing B's marker). A per-ledger mkdir lock around guard→commit closes it (pattern `ledger.sh:352`).
